claim.ru_maxrss_kib_derivation: ru_maxrss was never printed as an integer. The wrapper printed it twice, as 237.9 MB (ru_maxrss/1024) and 0.2324 GB (ru_maxrss/1024^2); intersecting the two roundings pins the unknown integer to 243637..243660 KiB, and 243648 (the midpoint) is the value this file converts. 237.9 MB is therefore MiB, not 237900 KiB: 237900 KiB would print 232.3 MB, not 237.9 MB
claim.unit_note: the source log prints '237.9 MB = 0.2324 GB' with both figures in binary-multiple units (MiB and GiB). Both conversions here are recomputed from the KiB value, not copied from the log: 243648 KiB / 1024^2 = 0.23236 GiB -> 0.2324, and 243648 KiB * 1024 / 1e9 = 0.249496 GB -> 0.2495. The misread '237.9e3 KiB' would give 0.2269 GiB and 0.2436 GB and is inconsistent with the log's own 0.2324
claim.precision: 4 significant figures only; the KiB integer is known to +/- ~13 KiB, the GB figures to the 4dp printed

method.how: the probe was run as a child of a Python wrapper; after the child exited the wrapper read resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss (KiB) plus ru_utime/ru_stime deltas, and timed the subprocess.run with time.perf_counter()
wrapper_output_verbatim: child user CPU = 2.182 s   sys CPU = 0.349 s
method.wrapper_code_status: NOT RECOVERABLE, stated rather than faked: the wrapper was supplied inline on the command line and was never written to disk. `grep -rn 'wrapper wall' /workspace /tmp` matches only evidence/t4/rung4_routeC_run.log itself, and no *.py/*.sh under /workspace or /tmp contains RUSAGE_CHILDREN. The four output lines above ARE verbatim; the code below is a reconstruction, not the original text
method.wrapper_code_reconstructed:
import resource, subprocess, sys, time
CMD = [sys.executable, "tools/host/sparse-probe/rung4_routeC_probe.py"]
r0 = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
t0 = time.perf_counter()
with open(sys.argv[1], "w") as fh:                      # log file: evidence/t4/rung4_routeC_run.log
    p = subprocess.run(CMD, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
r1 = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
print("--- wrapper ---")
print("child returncode = %d   wrapper wall = %.3f s" % (p.returncode, wall))
print("peak child RSS (ru_maxrss) = %.1f MB = %.4f GB" % (r1.ru_maxrss/1024.0, r1.ru_maxrss/1024.0/1024.0))
print("child user CPU = %.3f s   sys CPU = %.3f s" % (r1.ru_utime - r0.ru_utime, r1.ru_stime - r0.ru_stime))
method.reconstruction_verification: the reconstruction was re-run at schema-write time around a dummy child and reproduced the same four lines in the same order, labels and precision: '--- wrapper ---' / 'child returncode = 0   wrapper wall = 0.060 s' / 'peak child RSS (ru_maxrss) = 10.6 MB = 0.0103 GB' / 'child user CPU = 0.007 s   sys CPU = 0.002 s'
method.why_this_method: there is no /usr/bin/time and no ps in this container, so neither `time -v` nor RSS polling was available; an in-process getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) is the only option that yields a true peak rather than a sample

caveat: the number is the peak RSS of the whole child process tree as reported by RUSAGE_CHILDREN.ru_maxrss: it includes the interpreter, numpy/scipy imports and every page touched by the probe, not just the probe's own sparse factorisation (the report's own factor_memory_gb is 0.0164 GB, ~7% of the total). It is a single peak over the run's lifetime, not a memory profile: nothing here says when the peak occurred or what set it. Precision is also bounded: the log carries 4 significant figures, so the peak is 237.9 MB to that precision, not a byte count
